chapter: Connie's Inn, Duke Ellington and the Swingland band
title: Fletcher falls asleep writing; a wrong-key passage at a rehearsal
summary: Fletcher once fell asleep mid-chart, and the band suddenly lurched into another key at rehearsal, which broke the tension.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Many a times. In fact, I happened to have been on one of the rehearsals that he went to sleep and he was writing, and he forgot what key he was in, and all of the sudden, the band is swinging down, and they go into something else, and the guys looked, you know, one time, and Fletcher says, 'Oh my gosh, this was when I fell off asleep.' It
was funny. Man, everybody turned around and looked at each other. It didn't happen often, you know what I mean, but -- of course, the copyist didn't know this.
So he just wrote it out.
Like Flip Wilson says, what you see, is what you get.

But, this is what happened, and it go to be -- it was funny. It broke the spell. Everybody was tense, you know, they -- I think this was one of the tunes that they had played last, or next to last at the session, you know. I think usually on a session that time we'd do four tunes.
